resale_co.name: Certificate of Habitability (CH) for residential property sale, with Zoning Review and Fire Safety Certification
resale_co.issued_by: Town of Morristown Division of Housing & Property Maintenance, with a Zoning Review by the Zoning Officer
resale_co.valid_for: If the home is not occupied within 60 days of issuance, it must be reinspected and a new CH issued. A Temporary CH can be issued when repairs remain, for up to 30 days.
requirements: Habitability inspection of the exterior (fences, garage, sheds, chimneys, foundation, gutters, landscaping, paint, roof, sidewalks, stairs with railings for three or more treads, no pests)

Interior checks: asbestos encapsulated or removed, dry basement, bathroom ventilation, CO detectors, walls and ceilings, two working outlets in each habitable room, fireplace with proof of last flue cleaning, floors, furnace, GFCI outlets in kitchen and baths, water heater, kitchen ventilation to the outside, plumbing, smoke detectors, first-floor window sash locks
Satisfactory Zoning Review by the Zoning Officer for each dwelling unit
No CH while any construction permit is open
Occupancy Standard Form signed by seller, buyer and buyer's agent, returned to Housing & Property Maintenance
Purchaser and real estate licensee certifications about the maximum number of occupants
Pre-1981 dwellings that are not a primary residence must register with the Rent Leveling department
Fire extinguisher in each kitchen for 1-3 family homes (form still lists it)

fees.label: Certificate of Habitability, sale of condo, co-op, townhome, single-family or 2-family home (per unit)
Certificate of Habitability, one- and two-family house, each (Town Code 13-81)
fees.quote: One- and two-family house (consistent with R-1) (each)$160

fees.label: Habitability re-inspection, per instance
fees.quote: You must make these repairs and pay $80/unit for Re-Inspection and then the inspector will call you to schedule.

Zoning Review, sale of a 2-4 family home

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Application for Residential Property Sale & Fire Safety Certification Form and submit it with one payment (check, cash or money order payable to the Town of Morristown) covering the Zoning Review and Certificate of Habitability fees to the Division of Housing & Property Maintenance, 200 South Street, 2nd Floor, Morristown, NJ 07960. Zoning reviews the records; Housing then calls to schedule the inspection, which the owner or a designee must attend. Questions: 973-292-6700, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

evidence.quote: Before you sell any residential property in Morristown, you must obtain a Certificate of Habitability from the Division of Housing and Property Maintenance and a satisfactory Zoning Review from the Zoning Officer, for each dwelling unit.
Note: No CH will be issued while an open construction permit exist.
If you have questions about the approval process or how to calculate your fees, please call Housing & Property Maintenance (973) 292-6700 on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.
Sale of Condominium, Co-Op, Town Home, single-family or 2-family home.

If the premises for which a Certificate of Habitability has been issued is not occupied within 60 days of the issuance of said Certificate of Habitability, then the premises must be reinspected and a new Certificate of Habitability issued prior to occupancy.
All smoke detector and carbon monoxide fees are included in the inspection fees as per amendment to Ordinance No. O-4-08 adopted on March 11, 2008.
Residential Property Sale & Fire Safety Certification Application - PDF.pdf

resale_co.notes: Town Code Chapter 13 (Sections 13-80 to 13-83) was read through a text reader of ecode360. The CH fee for a 1-2 family sale is $160 per unit on both the application and in Section 13-81; the Code lists the reinspection fee as $80. The application's fee table shows Zoning Review flat fees of $50 (condo, co-op, townhome, single-family) and $75 (2-4 family). The rental tenancy-change application and the lead-based paint inspections in Section 13-74 apply to rentals only.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area (NFPA 72); 10-year sealed battery alarms for homes built before 1977; AC-powered alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas in homes with a fuel-burning device or attached garage (battery, hardwired or plug-in, UL 2034)

Portable fire extinguisher, 2A-10B:C, no more than 10 lbs, within 10 feet of the kitchen, mounted with the maker's bracket, top no more than 5 feet up, serviced and tagged in the past 12 months or with a recent receipt (form still lists it)
Seller signs an attestation that alarms are installed and working and all building permits are closed

fire_cert.notes: Morristown combines the sale smoke/CO certificate with the Certificate of Habitability on one application to Housing & Property Maintenance. Section 13-81 says smoke detector and carbon monoxide fees are included in the CH inspection fees, while Section 13-74(d) (amended 2024) lists $40 for a smoke/extinguisher/CO inspection, or $20 if combined with a CH; confirm whether anything is charged beyond the $160 CH fee. The Fire Official contact is from the state fire directory; the Town fire page did not render readable content. The application still requires a kitchen fire extinguisher; the state dropped it from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19).

other_items.label: Zoning Review
other_items.detail: A satisfactory Zoning Review by the Zoning Officer is required for each dwelling unit sold: $50 flat fee for a condo, co-op, townhome or single-family, $75 for a 2-4 family home (paid with the CH).

other_items.label: Open construction permits
other_items.detail: No Certificate of Habitability is issued while an open construction permit exists; check with the Building Department at 973-292-6712 or on the SDL Portal.

other_items.label: Rent Leveling registration
other_items.detail: Dwellings built before 1981 that are not a primary residence must register with the Rent Leveling department.
